prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Britain can be better. Labour’s 2015 manifesto is a plan for national renewal built on a simple truth: Britain only succeeds when working people succeed. It couples fairness with responsibility through a Budget Responsibility Lock: every policy is fully funded with no extra borrowing; the deficit will be cut every year; debt will fall with a surplus on the current budget as soon as possible; and major party manifestos will be audited by the OBR.

A stronger, fairer economy: Labour will balance the books with tough, fair choices—restoring the 50p top rate, introducing a 10p starting rate, abolishing non-dom status, and refusing rises in basic or higher Income Tax, National Insurance or VAT. It will clamp down on avoidance, reform HMRC, and direct proceeds like a Mansion Tax to an NHS Time to Care Fund.

Better work, better pay: Raise the National Minimum Wage to over £8 by 2019, promote the Living Wage via procurement and tax incentives, ban exploitative zero-hours contracts and agency undercutting, and scrap employment tribunal fees. Back small firms by cutting and freezing business rates, creating a British Investment Bank with regional banks, and tackling late payment. A long-term industrial strategy will drive productivity, build world-class infrastructure via a National Infrastructure Commission, support HS2 and northern rail, and lead a million green jobs with carbon-free electricity by 2030 and a stronger Green Investment Bank. Universal high-speed broadband and better mobile coverage will close digital gaps.

Mending broken markets: Freeze energy bills until 2017 while reforming the market, empower a tougher regulator, and drive home energy efficiency. Reform water to improve affordability. Put passengers first in rail—freeze fares next year, cap future rises, allow a public operator to compete for lines, and devolve bus powers with smart ticketing.

A world-class NHS and care: Recruit 20,000 nurses, 8,000 GPs and 3,000 midwives; guarantee GP appointments within 48 hours and one-week cancer tests; repeal the Health and Social Care Act, end the privatisation drive with an NHS preferred provider, cap profits, and integrate physical, mental and social care with parity for mental health. End 15‑minute care visits and recruit 5,000 home-care workers.

Opportunity for the next generation: Cut tuition fees to £6,000; guarantee quality apprenticeships for qualified school leavers; create a Compulsory Jobs Guarantee funded by a bank bonus tax; establish a gold-standard vocational route with Institutes of Technical Education; ensure English and Maths to 18.

Families, homes and security: Expand free childcare from 15 to 25 hours for working parents of three- and four‑year‑olds; double paternity leave and raise pay. Build at least 200,000 homes a year by 2020, curb land banking, give first-time buyers priority, and reform private renting with three‑year tenancies, rent-rise ceilings and a ban on letting fees. Abolish the Bedroom Tax; reform the Work Capability Assessment; keep the pension triple lock while restricting Winter Fuel Payments for the richest 5%.

Controlled immigration, fair rules: 1,000 extra border staff, full exit checks, a two‑year wait for EU benefit claims, English requirements for public‑facing staff, and tough action against exploitation and rogue agencies—alongside humane enforcement and support for refugees.

Safer communities and rights: Protect neighbourhood policing by replacing PCCs and safeguarding 10,000 officers; tackle child abuse and violence against women with stronger laws and stable refuge funding; overhaul Prevent to counter extremism while upholding liberties; zero‑tolerance for hate crime. Uphold the Human Rights Act, expand FOI, curb concentrated media power, implement Leveson, and keep Channel 4 public.

Power closer to people: An English Devolution Act will hand £30bn and real powers to city and county regions; a Constitutional Convention will renew the Union, replace the Lords with a Senate of the Nations and Regions, and extend votes to 16- and 17‑year‑olds.

Britain in the world: Lead in Europe by reforming, not leaving; lock any transfer of powers behind a referendum. Maintain strong Armed Forces, conduct a Strategic Defence and Security Review, retain a credible independent nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament, and lead on climate with a Paris deal toward net‑zero in the second half of the century. Keep 0.7% aid, fight poverty and inequality, and champion human rights.

Time for change: a country where everyone plays by the same rules, and Britain works again for working people.
